# PROCESS — cand_0004 (parent: cand_0003, champion val=0.660)

## Goal this iteration
cand_0003 (0.660) plateaued the type-contract prose lever. The plateau note said the next lever
is a WORKED discriminator, not more emphasis. Diagnosing THIS iteration's traces surfaced a
CONFLICT I had missed: cand_0003's own split/extract rule ("keep the piece as str EVEN WHEN an
example cell holds a datetime/number — the operation dictates str") is now the direct CAUSE of
two 0/3 failures. So this iteration is mostly CONSOLIDATION/NARROWING of rules that are
mis-firing, plus one bounded type rule. All edits in `task_template.md`; `prompt.md` untouched
(JOURNAL shows anti-fabrication prose there broke 50051).

Method: 5 parallel read-only diagnostic subagents read this iteration's `./trajectories/`
(type-cluster 325-44/30709; zero-score 53367/5192/50051/450-9; partial-pass 39046/51359/3911/
11842; remaining «redacted»; and a dedicated "pin the
split/extract boundary" agent on the passing anchor 50630 + 51958/110-2/41297). Edits applied
serially by me (surgical, single file).

## Ranked prose-fixable clusters (this iteration's traces)

### 1. CONFLICT / NARROW — split/extract str rule over-fires on named dates/numbers (HIGHEST)
Leverage: 2 hard 0/3 tasks + reinforces a third. cand_0003 edit C forced EVERY split/extract
piece to str. But 325-44 (`'Output'!A1:G10`) splits a filter string into **id columns** whose
reference is int/float (17 cells str-where-int), and 30709 (E6:E19) **"extract the dates"** whose
reference is real datetime (10 cells str-where-datetime). The agent's own code comments cite the
str rule as its rationale.
- **Edit 1** (split/extract bullet, rewritten + EXCEPTION bullet): the str default now applies
  only to generic "parts/sections" the instruction does NOT name as a typed value; ADDED
  exception — when the instruction's OWN request names the result a date/time/number/id/count,
  produce the real datetime/float/int. Keyed on what the instruction asks to PRODUCE, explicitly
  NOT on a date/number appearing in a header/source/example cell.
- Verify-the-fix: discriminator (a) validated by subagent against the passing anchor 50630
  ("split a sentence into three **parts**" → generic → str is gold, retains a trailing \xa0
  proving raw-substring). 325-44/30709 name their targets (ids / dates) → real type. Candidate
  discriminators (b) "token looks numeric/date" and (c) "substring vs whole-field" were tested
  and REJECTED — each misclassifies 50630 or 325-44.
- Blast radius: NARROWING (safe). Only passing split/extract task is 50630 (generic parts →
  str), which the reworded default preserves verbatim. No passing task extracts an
  instruction-named date/number yet keeps str (that would already fail). 51958 (convert/
  standardize) is whole-value, governed by the separate CONVERT rule — untouched.

### 2. CONSOLIDATION — recalc rule mis-applied: literalized a lookup into a volatile source
Leverage: 56996 (subagent "slam dunk") + 53367. The recalc block said "any formula whose inputs
are volatile, directly or transitively → write the LITERAL." 56996 asks to PUT a VLOOKUP for a
dropdown price; the price matrix is `=RANDBETWEEN(...)`. Following the rule, the agent snapshotted
cached numbers; the grader recalcs LibreOffice → new randoms → snapshot is stale (0/3). The
reference is a LIVE lookup that recalcs in lockstep. 53367 ("fix the broken formula") had the
correct live `SUMPRODUCT(...)>0` and REPLACED it with a Python `bool` → value/type mismatch.
- **Edit 2** (recalc block, rewritten): literalize only when YOUR ANSWER CELL's own formula is a
  non-recalcing TYPE (array/CSE, UNIQUE/FILTER/SORT, TEXTJOIN, AGGREGATE). Do NOT literalize just
  because a cell it READS is volatile/formula-driven — if the instruction asks to PUT/FIX a
  formula, or the answer must look up volatile/formula-driven cells, keep a LIVE ordinary formula
  so it recalcs in lockstep with the reference; a "fix the broken formula" corrected to an
  ordinary formula stays live (a Python bool/int grades as the wrong value/type).
- Verify-the-fix: matches both traces exactly (56996 snapshot-goes-stale; 53367 discarded the
  right live formula). Resolves the contradiction that produced the wrong action.
- Blast radius: BOUNDED. 47741 (passing) writes a LITERAL because TEXTJOIN doesn't recalc — the
  reworded rule still literalizes array/TEXTJOIN/AGGREGATE answer cells → 47741 unchanged.
  Plain-formula passers 55060 (IF), 55667 (INDEX/SUMPRODUCT), 58109 (SUMIFS/WORKDAY), CF_11072
  already keep live formulas → the rule reinforces their behavior. No passing task snapshots a
  volatile source (that would already fail).

### 3. KNOWLEDGE (bounded) — Python int where the reference holds a float
Leverage: 56427 (14 cells str/int-where-float) + reinforces 57232 (5 int-where-float) and 50051
(ROW() numbers likely float). Excel/recalc numbers are floats; the agent wrote Python int.
- **Edit 3** (type-matching section, new bullet): a number produced by an Excel formula/recalc is
  a float; when a worked-example/reference cell in the range holds a whole number as a float
  (28.0, 66.0), write your computed answer as a float too — match the example cell's numeric type
  when one is present on any copy.
- Verify-the-fix: 56427's worked-example cells are floats; 325-44's specialtyId reference is
  66.0 (float). Directly closes the int-vs-float type gap.
- Blast radius: BOUNDED. Fires only when an example/reference cell in the range is a float, so it
  only flips currently-failing int-where-float cases; count tasks whose example cells are int
  (e.g. 39046 F) keep int. Live-formula answers (Edit 2) get the float type for free.

## Deliberately SKIPPED (documented)
- **5192, 450-9**: gold not derivable from visible data. 5192's two worked examples contradict
  (`CH02A1456`→drops trailing A vs `MH2A215`→keeps A); the agent matched BOTH stated examples yet
  0/3, so the true rule is undetermined. 450-9's reference is a hand-authored demo (literal 'etc'
  at a fixed row, blank A/B below it, 168 rows squeezed into a 150-row target). Prose can't fix
  without hardcoding gold.
- **39046, 51359, 3911**: gold provably INCONSISTENT across copies (identical inputs → different
  pre-filled answers; or a non-unique scarce-note allocation the instruction never disambiguates).
  The agent's interpretation is defensible and passes the copies it passes; any prose chasing them
  risks regressing a passing copy.
- **11842, 55931**: the governing rule already exists (cand_0003 edit B1 "use the sheet's own
  COUNTIF/summary formula, don't re-count in Python"; edit B2 "no-match is not a licence to emit
  #N/A"). The agent read and skipped it → known-but-broken, not a knowledge gap (adding prose
  won't change behavior). Residual causes (half-day divide-by-2; diff sign direction) are ambiguous.
- **56637**: cand_0002 already regressed here off the correct in-sheet =IF; the overwrite-of-
  independent-C/D-cells fix needs a range-semantics rule with UNBOUNDED blast radius on sheet-level
  fills. Too risky this iteration.

## Building on prior RESULTS
- Kept ALL of cand_0003's accepted edits as the base; Edit 1 NARROWS its edit C (which over-fired),
  Edit 2 CONSOLIDATES its recalc block, Edit 3 is additive.
- Did NOT re-add prompt.md anti-fabrication prose (broke 50051, cand_0001) nor any global
  "text→plain string" type rule (broke 73-45, cand_0001/0002). prompt.md untouched.

## Constraints honored
- Edited ONLY task_template.md; prompt.md unchanged. No adapter/harness/scorer/env edits.
- All load-bearing placeholders present/unchanged: {instruction} {spreadsheet_path}
  {spreadsheet_content} {instruction_type} {answer_position} {output_path} {max_turns}.
- No task-specific id/value/date/answer hardcoded; every rule is a general condition.
- 3 edits: 1 NARROWING + 1 CONSOLIDATION + 1 BOUNDED-additive. No global decision/permission rule
  loosened.
